logp.method_description: Log P was calculated as the decimal logarithm of the ratio of the solute concentrations in n-octanol and in water after partition equilibrium. A solution of each complex (10 mL) was mixed with 20 mL of octanol and 30 mL of distilled water in a 250-mL flask. The mixture was mixed with a mechanical shaker for 30 min. The solution was then allowed to stand for 24 h before separating the aqueous and organic phases. After separation, 3 mL of solution was collected from each phase, and the concentrations of the compound were determined by UV–visible spectroscopy. The spectrophotometric UV–visible (log P determinations) was determined using the wavelength corresponding to the maximum absorption of each compound in different media. In each case, the concentration of each sample was determined from a calibration plot with four known concentrations in the organic and aqueous phases. In each case, a straight line was obtained according to the equation y = mx + c, where x is the concentration of solute (mol L-1) and y is the absorbance at the wavelength of maximum absorbance.
